question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy-z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix parametrized by $r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+2t\,k$ for $t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=2t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,k \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy-z\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt-z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-2t\cdot 2\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}9{sin}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{2}⁡t-4t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}9-4t\,dt \\  & =(9t-2{t}^{2}){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}(9-\pi )\end{aligned}
$$
